blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Policy enforcement for LLM agents has shifted from single-turn content moderation to compound, application-specific policies evaluated over multi-turn transcripts and tool-call trajectories. Fine-tuned guardrail models are efficient but degrade on compound policies, and while LLM-as-a-judge approaches achieve higher accuracy, they incur high inference cost and tend to produce unstable predictions. Neurosymbolic methods offer a natural alternative, decomposing the policy into narrow neural decisions composed under explicit logic. However, existing symbolic layers lack the required expressiveness and are optimized against fixed data rather than the policy itself. To address this, we introduce SCOPE, which compiles a policy into an executable program of neural predicates executed by small models, deterministic extractors, and code that composes their outputs. The program is optimized jointly with its training data, using adversarial generation of counterexamples that target where the program deviates from the policy. We evaluate SCOPE on a benchmark of real-world policy tasks against prompt optimization, task decomposition, and workflow generation methods, achieving the highest average accuracy across tasks and models. Programs optimized with the weakest executor transfer to other models without further optimization. This allows them to be deployed in production on inexpensive models, where they reach accuracy comparable to frontier reasoning models. Unlike these monolithic models, SCOPE produces substantially more stable predictions, and each verdict is interpretable through the predicate outputs that produced it. Additionally, we validate the key components of our method through an ablation study. SCOPE thus enables reliable, interpretable, and efficient policy enforcement at production scale.
blocks.zh: 对LLM代理人的政策执行已经从单回合内容节制转向复合、具体应用政策,对多回合记录和工具调用轨迹进行评价。 精细的护栏模型是高效的,但因复合政策而退化,虽然LLM-as-a-judge方法的精确度较高,但它们的推论成本很高,往往产生不稳定的预测。 Neurosymbolic方法提供了一个自然的替代方法,将政策分解成由明确逻辑构成的狭义神经决定. 然而,现有的象征性层缺乏所需的表达性,是对照固定数据而不是政策本身来优化的. 为了解决这个问题,我们引入了SCOPE,它将一个政策汇编成一个可执行的程序,其中包含由小模型执行的神经上游,决定提取器,以及构成其输出的代码. 方案与其培训数据一起进行优化,使用对抗式生成的反实例,在方案偏离政策的地方设定目标. 我们对照快速优化、任务分解和工作流程生成方法,在现实世界政策任务基准上评价SCOPE,实现不同任务和模式最高平均准确性。 程序优化后最弱的执行器转移到其他模型,而无需进一步优化. 这使得它们能够被部署在廉价的模型上,达到与前沿推理模型相当的精度. 与这些单体模型不同的是,SCOPE能产生相当稳定的预测,每个判断可以通过产生它的上游输出来解释. 此外,我们通过消化研究验证我们方法的关键组成部分。 因此,SCOPE能够在生产规模上可靠、可解释和有效地执行政策。

blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models are increasingly deployed to enforce the policies of the
organizations that run them, from content rules [ 37 , 31 , 98 ] and regulatory obligations [ 17 ] to application-specific constraints
on permissible system behavior [ 89 , 54 ] . As these applications
advance from single-turn moderation to multi-turn assistants and tool-using
agents, both the policies and the inputs they govern grow more complex. The unit
of judgment becomes a long transcript [ 33 , 94 ] , a structured plan [ 35 ] , or an agent trajectory [ 89 , 12 ] rather than a single
message, and a modern policy is rarely one flat category: it bundles conditions,
exceptions, counts, and interactions that must be assessed together [ 33 ] . Adhering to such a policy is therefore both critical and
hard [ 94 ] , as the verdict turns on a compound, context-dependent specification rather
than a single surface feature, where one overlooked clause produces a false
violation or a missed obligation.

The most direct approach uses a language model as the policy classifier itself.
Its principal advantage is generality: any policy that can be expressed in
natural language can be enforced without a predefined taxonomy [ 33 , 67 , 62 ] . This approach takes two forms. The first trains a custom
classifier on the task, typically a small fine-tuned guardrail model [ 37 , 31 , 98 , 24 ] . Such models are fast and
inexpensive, and on a single, well-scoped rule they match far larger models [ 54 ] . Their capacity is the ceiling, so accuracy falls as a policy
compounds interacting conditions beyond what one model resolves in a
single pass [ 20 ] . The second prompts a frontier model with the
policy at runtime and reads its verdict, the paradigm known as LLM-as-a-judge [ 101 , 50 ] . While it is more capable on the compound case, its predictions are unstable [ 30 , 76 , 7 ] , with variance rising with the number of clauses in the
input [ 57 ] . Further, even dedicated reasoning models collapse past a complexity threshold rather than scaling through it [ 79 ] . Finally, its inference cost and latency make it impractical at production scale, where high-throughput classification is required. The first form is thus reliable only on simple policies, while the second is neither stable nor scalable.

blocks.en:
A neurosymbolic approach is the natural alternative. Such methods pair neural
components that supply semantic judgment with a symbolic layer that composes
their outputs under explicit logic [ 52 , 49 ] . Because each sub-decision is narrowly scoped and the composition is explicit, the verdict is more stable than a monolithic judgment [ 46 ] . As narrow sub-decisions are simpler [ 41 , 102 , 70 ] , they can also be answered by small models, which makes the system cheaper to run. The weakness of existing methods lies in the symbolic layer itself, along two axes. The first is expressiveness: checklists [ 46 , 15 ] , weighted rule sets [ 92 , 58 ] , and compiled Boolean or probabilistic rules [ 12 , 38 , 93 ] cannot express the conditional, iterative, and computational structure that complex real-world use cases carry. The second is bias: a learned or synthesized layer is fit to a proxy for the policy, not to the policy itself, whether a rule set tuned to its training samples [ 92 ] , a program searched against a static benchmark [ 99 , 34 ] , or a function verified against self-generated tests and specifications [ 56 ] .

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduce SCOPE (Symbolic Composition Over Predicates and Extractors), which compiles a natural-language policy into a neurosymbolic program: neural predicates resolved by weak models, cheap sub-frontier models served without extended reasoning, deterministic extractors for exact computation, and executable code that composes their outputs. Expressiveness is met by the composition being code: it expresses the structure of real-world policies naturally, which rule-based formalisms capture only at low fidelity. Bias is mitigated by how the training data is built. Rather than relying only on a static training set, the search draws on an adversary that repeatedly generates counterexamples targeting where the current program departs from the specification [ 80 ] , and the program is revised against them.
Counterexamples are produced by the adversary at two levels: local drift, where a predicate no longer tracks the clause it transcribes, and global drift, where the decomposition as a whole misses a predicate or misroutes an interaction between clauses. Each counterexample is labeled by a strong teacher applying the full policy, and the cost is paid once at compilation. The unit of optimization is thus not a single rule [ 54 ] but the compound policy: each round adds counterexamples and updates both the predicate formulations and the code that composes them. The converged program runs entirely on weak models, so it is cheap to serve. Each verdict is attributable to the predicate outputs behind it rather than a post-hoc rationale, and, being built from narrow classifications, is more stable than a monolithic judgment.

反例由对手在两个层面产生:局部漂移,上游不再跟踪它所转录的条款;全球漂移,整体上分解缺失了上游或错序条款之间的相互作用。 每个反例均由应用全方位政策的强师标出标签,费用一经整理即可支付. 因此,优化的单位不是一个单一的规则[54]而是一个复合政策:每回合都添加了反例并同时更新了上游配方和构成它们的代码. 收缩后的程序完全运行在弱模型上,因此服务价格低廉. 每项判决都归因于其背后的上游产出,而不是事后的理由,而且根据狭隘的分类,比单一判断更为稳定。

blocks.en: We release a benchmark of four policy-enforcement tasks, derived from public benchmarks or modeled on deployed agentic systems. The tasks span long agent traces, multi-turn counting, critic auditing, and dynamic multi-label outputs. SCOPE attains the best accuracy in most task-executor settings, outperforming prompt optimization, neurosymbolic methods, and workflow generation. Its advantage grows as the executor weakens. Once a policy is compiled into predicates a weak model can answer without reasoning, accuracy becomes largely insensitive to the choice of executor. Programs compiled with our weakest executor transfer directly to other models, matching frontier reasoning models at a fraction of the inference cost. They are also far more stable: where reasoning models flip a substantial share of their verdicts across repeated runs, SCOPE’s predictions remain nearly fixed, and each verdict traces to the predicate outputs that produced it. Ablations confirm that adversarial generation is central to these gains. More broadly, SCOPE shows that natural-language policies can be compiled rather than interpreted, turning policy enforcement from an opaque judgment delegated to a frontier model into a program that can be optimized, inspected, and deployed at scale.
blocks.zh: 我们公布了四项政策执行任务的基准,这些任务取自公共基准或以部署的代理系统为模型。 这些任务跨越长期代理追踪、多回合计数、批评者审计和动态多标签产出。 SCOPE在大多数任务执行器设置中达到最佳准确性,表现优于即时优化,神经同位素方法,以及工作流程生成. 它的优势随着执行者的削弱而增长. 一旦将政策汇编成上游,一个薄弱的模型可以不推理地回答,准确性就在很大程度上对执行者的选择不敏感了。 程序与我们最弱的执行器直接转移到其他模型一起编译,匹配前沿推理模型,成本为推论成本的一小部分. 这些模型也更加稳定:推理模型在反复重复的循环中翻转了它们判决的一大部分,而SCOPE的预测仍然几乎固定,每个判决都跟随产生它的上游产出。 违约证实,对抗性一代是这些收益的核心。 更广泛地说,SCOPE表明,自然语言政策可以编译,而不是解释,将政策执行从不透明的判决转变为前沿模式,转变为可大规模优化、检查和部署的方案。

blocks.en:
Policy enforcement asks a classifier to decide whether an input satisfies a policy written in prose. Modern deployments impose requirements that earlier content moderation did not. Policies may involve complex combinations of conditions, exceptions, counts, and interactions that must be assessed together, potentially over long inputs such as multi-turn transcripts [ 33 , 94 ] , structured plans [ 35 ] , or agent trajectories [ 89 , 12 ] , in which the evidence deciding the verdict occupies a small fraction of the context. cheap, because the enforcer gates every interaction and its cost is paid on each
one [ 54 , 100 ] , and consistent, because a verdict that
shifts with position or surface form is not an enforcement of the policy at all [ 86 , 21 , 96 ] .

blocks.en:
Existing approaches trade expressiveness against cost and consistency. Blocklists and
regular expressions are the least expressive: deterministic, perfectly
repeatable, and nearly free to run, but blind to anything their patterns do not
literally contain [ 82 , 60 ] . Compact models fine-tuned on a single
narrow task judge semantics rather than surface form [ 37 , 31 , 98 , 24 , 51 ] , and need no annotation once their
training data is synthesized from the policy text alone [ 54 , 78 , 16 ] ; their capacity is the ceiling,
and accuracy falls once a policy bundles interacting conditions that a single forward pass must resolve together [ 20 , 57 ] . Guardrails conditioned on a policy supplied at runtime [ 33 , 66 , 19 , 43 ] are expressive and cheap, but, being far smaller than frontier models, they share the capacity ceiling above and still err on multi-clause policies [ 33 ] . Frontier LLM-as-a-judge [ 101 , 50 ] is the most expressive and is accurate on compound policies. Yet it is the least consistent [ 30 , 76 ] , variance rising with the number of clauses [ 57 ] , and the most expensive, a frontier call for every gated interaction. Prompt optimization [ 103 , 71 , 91 , 88 , 40 , 65 , 97 , 13 , 1 , 47 ] can tune the judge’s instructions, but as the verdict of a monolithic judge still comes from a single call, it inherits the same limitations.

Scope breaks this trade-off. A policy is compiled into a program whose atoms
are predicates resolved by small models and whose composition is explicit code,
so the expressiveness of a frontier judge is obtained at the cost and the
repeatability of a weak classifier: no strong-model call is made at inference, the
composition is deterministic, and both the predicates and the code composing them
are optimized against the policy itself.

blocks.en:
Neurosymbolic methods pair neural components, which supply semantic judgment,
with a symbolic layer that composes their outputs. Keeping the composition
explicit rather than folding it into a network’s weights makes the verdict
readable and checkable, and captures procedural structure that a single forward
pass does not [ 10 ] . Two axes organize what follows: how expressive the symbolic layer is, and how much of the method is learned rather than fixed in advance. On the first axis, the layer ranges from a logic program [ 52 , 49 ] to executable code [ 22 , 11 , 48 , 29 , 84 , 83 , 14 ] , which, unlike a logic program whose rules are written by hand and whose neural predicates are trained through its inference, can be written and revised by an LLM and can call models directly on intermediate results.
On the second axis, both the composition and the neural predicates it calls may be either given or learned.
Classical differentiable programs fix the structure and train the predicates through it [ 52 , 49 , 4 ] , while others search for the structure as well: over a typed functional language [ 85 ] , guided by neural relaxations [ 77 ] , or over programs whose nodes invoke a language model [ 99 , 34 , 87 ] .

blocks.en:
Existing methods have stayed on one side of each axis at a time. One line
derives a symbolic structure, generated from the policy or fit to data, but over a restricted formalism: a
count over atomic yes/no questions [ 46 , 15 ] , linear weights over
natural-language rules [ 58 , 92 ] , a probabilistic circuit over trajectory
predicates [ 12 ] , or a logical encoding checked by an SMT solver [ 3 ] .
Such a formalism is tractable to derive precisely because it is restricted, and for the same reason it cannot make which question is asked depend on earlier answers, count occurrences over spans extracted from the input, or repeat a check over parts of the input selected at run time, structures that real policies commonly contain.
The other line
writes the composition as code, gaining that expressiveness, but leaves the
program fixed: hand-authored rails [ 73 ] , a synthesized function
verified against self-generated tests and specifications [ 56 , 104 ] , or a program emitted
per task whose generator is never tuned against the policy [ 36 , 89 ] . Its predicates are frozen prompts, so one
that drifts from the clause it transcribes stays drifted. SCOPE combines both lines: its composition is ordinary Python, and its structure and predicates are optimized jointly against the policy.

blocks.en:
SCOPE searches for an executable program π \pi that reproduces the verdicts of a natural-language policy when every predicate is answered by a weak model. The policy assigns each input, such as a conversation or an agent trace, a label from a fixed set or, for multi-label tasks, a set of labels. As detailed in Section 3.1 , the program consists of predicates , classification questions answered by a weak LLM, and extractors , deterministic functions over the input, combined by Python composition code. We denote by s ⁡ ( π , D ) s(\pi,D) the score of π \pi on a pool D D , measured as accuracy for single-label tasks and the Jaccard index for multi-label tasks.
Only a small seed pool D 0 D_{0} of human-labeled samples is given. During optimization, an adversarial process generates new samples that target where the program may depart from the policy and adds them to the pool. The program is thus fit to the policy rather than to a fixed dataset.

blocks.en: 3.1 The Decomposition Program
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 分解方案

blocks.en:
A program consists of predicates, extractors, and composition code. A predicate is
a natural-language classification question with a fixed label set, typically
binary. An extractor is a deterministic function that returns a value, a span, or
a list of spans from the input. The composition code is a Python function that
invokes extractors to select spans, applies predicates to them, and maps the
resulting labels to a verdict. Predicates do not specify their input; the
composition code determines the text to which each predicate is applied. The same
predicate may therefore be applied to the full input, to a span within it, or
repeatedly within a single sample.

带有固定标签的自然语言分类问题,一般
二进制. 提取器是返回值、跨度或

因此,上游可适用于其内部的全部输入,或

blocks.en:
Expressing the composition as code allows the program to mirror the structure of the policy. A predicate can be restricted to the region its question concerns, such as one section of a long input, or applied multiple times to different parts of the input. Although predicate label sets are fixed, the program can handle tasks whose label set varies per sample or that require multiple labels, by determining how predicates are applied to the sample’s candidates and how their outputs form the final prediction. Predicates can also be invoked conditionally on earlier answers. Counts and thresholds can be computed exactly by deterministic extractors, rather than estimated by a model [ 22 , 11 ] .
Appendix A presents a complete program.
blocks.zh:
将构成表示为代码,使程序能够反映政策的结构. 上游可限于该区域的问题关切,例如长输入的一节,或多次适用于输入的不同部分。 虽然上游标签集是固定的,但程序可以通过确定上游如何适用于样本候选人以及其产出如何构成最终预测,来处理每个样本的标签集不同或需要多个标签的任务. 也可以有条件地以先前的答案援引预测。 计数和阈值可以精确地由决定提取器计算,而不是由模型[22,11]估算出.
附 录 A呈现一个完整的程序.

blocks.en: During the search, every predicate call is answered by an executor , a sub-frontier model run with reasoning disabled and instructed to return only the label. The executor is chosen to match the capability of the models intended for deployment. A predicate that the executor cannot answer reliably is likely to be reworded or split into simpler questions. The structure of the program therefore adapts to the capability of the executor, and weaker executors yield programs with more predicates (Figure 3 b). Since the executor receives only a predicate and its input, without the policy, each predicate must be self-contained, stating the definitions, scope, and exceptions of the clause it encodes.
blocks.zh: 在搜索过程中,每个上游呼叫都由一个执行者回答,一个次前沿模式运行,推理被禁并指示只返回标签. 选择执行人是为了与准备部署的模型的能力相匹配。 一个被执行人无法可靠回答的前提很可能被重新措辞或被分成更简单的问题. 因此,程序的结构适应了执行者的能力,而较弱的执行者则以更高的上游来生成程序(图3b). 由于执行者只收到一个上游及其输入,而没有政策,每个上游必须自成一体,说明它编码的条款的定义、范围和例外。

blocks.en: This choice of executor is motivated by cost, stability, and traceability. Sub-frontier models are considerably cheaper to run than frontier models, yet capable of answering narrowly scoped questions without any training. Running without reasoning is intended to keep predictions stable across runs (Section 5.1 ). Finally, executing a program on a sample produces a trace: the ordered sequence of predicate calls, each with the exact text it received and the label it returned. Traces make every verdict attributable to specific predicate outputs, and they are the primary signal for the search. The optimizer uses them to localize failures (Section 3.2 ), and the local adversary uses them to observe the inputs a predicate actually receives (Section 3.3 ).
blocks.zh: 选择执行人是出于成本、稳定性和可追踪性。 边疆模式比边疆模式要便宜得多,但能够不经过任何培训地回答范围狭窄的问题。 毫无推理地运行是为了使预测在整个运行中保持稳定(第5.1节)。 最后,在样本上执行一个程序会产生一个痕迹:命令的上游呼叫序列,每个序列都有它收到的准确文本和它返回的标签. Traces根据特定的上游产出做出每个判断,它们是搜索的主要信号. 优化者使用它们来定位故障(第3.2节),而当地对手使用它们来观察一个上游实际收到的输入(第3.3节)。

blocks.en: 3.2 Optimizer
blocks.zh: 3.2 优化剂

blocks.en: The search starts from the undecomposed task: a single predicate, the policy itself, applied to the full input. Before the first round, the teacher writes a rationale for each seed sample. At round t t , the teacher labels the samples the adversaries added in the previous round (Section 3.3 ), and the current program is executed on D t D_{t} . The analyzer receives the policy, the program, and, for every sample, the predicted verdict, the gold label, its rationale, and the trace. Supervision exists only for the final verdict, so the analyzer infers which calls caused a failure by working backward: it replays the composition code on the recorded predicate labels, finds the labels that would have had to differ to produce the gold verdict, and inspects the text those calls received. Each failure is thus attributed to a predicate whose wording does not encode its clause, or to composition code that misencodes the policy. Correctly classified samples with similar rationales serve as a contrast set for checking candidate fixes against regressions.
blocks.zh: 搜索从未分解的任务开始:一个单一的上游,政策本身,应用于全部输入. 在第一轮比赛前,老师会写出每个种子样本的理由. 在 t 回合中, 老师给上一轮( 第3.3节)中加入的对手标出标本, 而当前程序则在 D t D_{t 上执行 。 分析师接收了政策,程序,并且,对于每一个样本,预测的判决,金色标签,其原理,以及追踪. 监督只存在于最终判决中,因此分析者推断称因工作后退而导致失败:它重放所记录的上游标签上的成分代码,发现为了产生黄金判决而不得不不同的标签,并检查所收到呼叫的文本. 因此,每次失败都归因于其措辞没有编码其条款的上游,或归因于对政策进行错误编码的构成代码。 对具有类似理由的样本进行正确分类,作为对照对照,对照回归情况检查候选人的确定办法。

blocks.en: The analyzer then recommends revisions: rewording or splitting a predicate, adding or removing a predicate or extractor, moving a condition between a predicate and an extractor, or rewriting the composition code. Each recommendation must be grounded in a clause, definition, or exception of the policy. A revision justified only by a phrase observed in a sample would fit the pool rather than the policy, and is excluded. The decomposer treats these recommendations as proposals and weighs them against the search history: previous programs and their scores, the revisions applied in the last round, and revisions already tried from the current program without improvement. When recent rounds do not improve the score, the search backtracks to the best program found so far, and the decomposer must pursue a substantially different direction, which prevents cycling among similar programs. The search terminates when s ⁡ ( π , D t ) s(\pi,D_{t}) reaches a threshold τ \tau , or after K K rounds. Since D t D_{t} grows across rounds, its scores are not comparable between rounds, so the returned program is the candidate with the highest score s ⁡ ( π , D 0 ) s(\pi,D_{0}) on the fixed seed pool.

blocks.en: 3.3 Adversarial Generators
blocks.zh: 3.3 辅助发电机

blocks.en: Optimizing against a fixed pool rewards fitting the pool: a policy condition that the pool rarely exercises can be omitted at little cost in accuracy, and the pool provides no signal to restore it. SCOPE therefore grows the pool adversarially. After each revision, two adversaries compare the policy with the current program and generate samples on which the two are likely to disagree. Supervision thus concentrates where the program is wrong, analogously to counterexample-guided synthesis [ 80 ] , with the policy as the specification. Both adversaries see the current pool, including D 0 D_{0} and all previously generated samples, so new samples stay consistent with it and avoid redundancy.
blocks.zh: 与固定的游泳池相比,优化奖励适合游泳池:一个政策条件是,游泳池很少能够以很少的准确性成本省去锻炼,游泳池没有提供恢复游泳池的信号。 因此,SCOPE会以对抗性的方式增加总汇。 每次修订后,有两名对手将政策与目前的程序进行比较,并生成两人可能不同意的样本. 因此,监督集中在程序错误的地方,类似地用于反例制导合成[80],以政策为规格. 两个对手都看到现在的池子,包括D0 D_{0}和所有以前产生的样本,所以新的样本都与它保持一致并避免冗余.

blocks.en: The adversaries operate at two levels. The systemic adversary targets global drift: a clause, exception, or interaction between clauses that the program as a whole misrepresents. It reads the full program and generates inputs on which the composition omits or misroutes part of the policy (Appendix E.1 ). The local adversary targets local drift: a single predicate that no longer tracks the clause it encodes. It examines one predicate at a time, together with traces of the inputs that predicate receives, and generates inputs that probe where its wording diverges from the clause (Appendix E.2 ). Each sample is generated with an intended label and a justification. The teacher, applying the full policy, labels it without seeing either, and the sample enters the pool only if the two labels agree, so every admitted sample reflects two separate readings of the policy.
blocks.zh: 对手在两个层面运作。 系统性对手针对全球漂移:一个条款,例外,或者整个程序歪曲的条款之间的相互作用. 它读取了完整的程序并生成了输入,其中成分会省略或误入部分策略(Appendix E.1. 本地对手瞄准本地漂移:一个单一的上游,不再跟踪它编码的条款. 它一次审查一个上游,连同上游接收的投入的痕迹,并生成其措辞与条款相去甚远的投入(附录E.2.)。 每个样本都附有预定标签和理由。 老师应用了完整的政策,没有看到两者之一就贴出标签,只有在两个标签一致的情况下,样本才进入池中,因此每个被录取的样本都反映了政策的两个单独的读取.

blocks.en: Escalation. Inspired by the counting policies of DynaGuard [ 33 ] , the input is a customer-support dialogue. Escalation is warranted when the user re-raises the same unresolved intent at least three times, verbatim or rephrased. A turn that adds a new constraint, question, or information does not count, so each turn must be compared semantically with the earlier ones. The label is True when the agent’s final reply escalates exactly when warranted (Appendix E.2 ).

blocks.en: 4.2 Baseline methods
blocks.zh: 4.2 基线方法

blocks.en: Prompt optimization. To separate the effect of structural decomposition from prompt optimization alone, we compare against two optimizers implemented in DSPy [ 40 , 39 ] : GEPA [ 1 ] and MIPROv2 [ 65 ] . Both improve a fixed task description by rewriting it (MIPROv2 also selects few-shot demonstrations), without decomposing the task. GEPA maintains a pool of candidate instructions. It reflects on execution traces and metric feedback on a minibatch of training instances to propose a revision, and selects the next candidate to mutate from the Pareto front over training instances. MIPROv2 is a Bayesian optimizer that jointly searches over instructions and bootstrapped few-shot demonstrations, using a proposal model to draft candidate instructions grounded in a summary of the training data. For a controlled comparison, both optimize on the training pool that SCOPE starts from, use the same executor model, and are scored on the same held-out test set.
blocks.zh: 即时优化. 为了将结构分解的效果与快速优化单独区分开来,我们比较了DSPy[40,39]中执行的两个优化器:GEPA [1]和MIPROv2 [65]. 两者都通过重写来改进固定的任务描述(MIPROv2也选择了几发的演示),而没有拆解任务. GEPA保持一系列候选人指示。 它反思了执行的痕迹和对一小批培训案例的衡量反馈,以提议修订,并从Pareto前线挑选下一个候选人,而不是培训案例。 MIPROv2是贝叶斯人的一个优化器,它联合搜索指令,并用一款基于培训数据摘要的提案模型来起草候选人说明。 为了进行有控制的比较,既优化了SCOPE从开始的训练池,使用相同的执行器模型,又在同一被搁置的测试集上得分.

blocks.en:
Task decomposition. We evaluate Scope with three executor models: gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.4-mini [ 63 ] , and gemini-3.5-flash [ 27 ] , each configured with reasoning disabled. We compare against two neurosymbolic task-decomposition baselines.
CheckEval [ 46 ] is a checklist-based LLM-as-a-judge that decomposes the policy into binary yes/no questions seeded from a manual list and expanded through LLM diversification and elaboration, and scores each sample by the proportion of “yes” answers.
RLIE [ 92 ] instead induces a set of natural-language rules from labeled samples, refined iteratively and combined by a logistic regression. By construction, both methods support only binary labels, so we evaluate them only on the binary tasks.
blocks.zh:
任务分解. 我们用三种执行器模型来评价范围:gpt-5.4-nano,gpt-5.4-mini [63];和Gemini-3.5-flash [27],每个模型配置的推理功能被禁用. 我们比较了两个神经相通的任务分解基线.
CheckEval[46]是一个基于清单的LLM-as-a-judge,将政策分解为二进制是/否问题,从一个人工清单中引出,并通过LLM多样化和阐述加以扩展,并按“是”答案的比例对每个样本进行评分。
RLIE [92] 反而从标注的样本中诱导出一套自然语言规则,经过反复的精炼并结合了物流回归. 通过构建,两种方法都只支持二进制标签,所以我们只评价二进制任务.

blocks.en: Automated workflow generation. We compare against AFlow [ 99 ] , an automated agentic-workflow optimizer, which runs Monte-Carlo tree search over programs that orchestrate multiple LLM calls through reusable operators. Like Scope it searches over executable programs rather than a single prompt, but its search space is open-ended rather than a decomposition of the policy. Since Scope and all other baselines were allowed to emit nothing but the label, we restricted AFlow to the Custom operator and disabled chain-of-thought answer generation. Notably, the instructions AFlow writes for the Custom operator may themselves elicit intermediate reasoning, on which the final label can be conditioned. This is inherent to the method, so we left it in place, thus allowing AFlow a capability that the other methods did not have.
blocks.zh: 自动化工作流程生成. 我们比较AFlow[99],一个自动代理-工作流优化器,它运行蒙特-卡罗树搜索比通过可重复使用的操作器来协调多个LLM调用的程序. 与“范围”一样,它搜索的是可执行程序,而不是单一的即时程序,但其搜索空间是开放的,而不是政策的分解。 由于“范围”和所有其他基线仅被允许发出标签,因此我们把AFlow限制在自定义操作员和禁用思维链式答案生成器。 值得注意的是,AFlow为自定义操作员撰写的指令本身可能引出中间推理,最终标签可以以此为条件. 这是方法固有的,所以我们把它留在原地,从而允许AFlow拥有其他方法没有的能力.

blocks.en: 4.3 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 4.3 详细执行情况

blocks.en:
All core models in the decomposition process (the analyzer, decomposer, adversarial sample generators and teacher) run Claude Opus 4.8 [ 6 ] in an agentic loop. The agent SDK [ 5 ] provides file access, allowing the models to (i) read long records from disk on demand rather than receiving them inline, keeping prompts compact for tasks with inputs spanning tens of thousands of characters, and (ii) generate very long samples by editing seeds, which is difficult to accomplish in standard inference mode.
The executor models run the predicates, producing only a label, without a rationale.
blocks.zh:
分解过程中的所有核心模型(分析器,分解器,对抗样品生成器和老师)都以代理环来运行克洛德·奥普斯 4.8 [6]. 代理SDK [5] 提供文件访问,允许模型(一)按需要从磁盘上读取长记录,而不是接受其内接,对包含数以万计字符输入的任务保持提示紧凑,并(二)通过编辑种子生成非常长的样本,这在标准推论模式下难以完成.
执行器模型运行上游,只产生标签,没有理由.

blocks.en: For each task, we split the human-annotated set into training and test portions. The training portion forms the initial pool D 0 D_{0} . The test portion is used only for the final evaluation. The search runs for at most K = 8 K=8 iterations, and stops early once accuracy on the current training pool reaches τ = 0.98 \tau=0.98 . In each iteration, the systemic adversary generates at most three samples and each predicate-local adversary adds at most one, so that adversarial samples enrich the human-labeled pool without dominating it.
blocks.zh: 对于每项任务,我们把附加说明的成套设备分为培训和测试部分。 训练部分组成了最初的游泳池D 0 D_{0}. 测试部分仅用于最终评价. 搜索最多为K=8K=8次重复,一旦当前训练池的准确度达到0.98\tau=0.98,就提前停止。 在每个迭代中,系统对抗者最多生成三个样本,每个上游-局部对抗者最多会添加一个样本,这样对抗性样本就可以丰富被人类标注的池子而不会支配它.

blocks.zh: 5 结果和分析

blocks.en: Figure 2 reports test accuracy for the four tasks under the three executor models, with the exact numbers detailed in Table 6 (Appendix D ). All reported numbers are averaged over three independent runs of the optimization process and three repetitions of the final test evaluation, for a total of 9 measurements. Both CheckEval and RLIE support binary predictions only and therefore apply to Escalation and Plan alone.
blocks.zh: 图2报告测试三种执行模式下的四项任务的准确性,具体数字详见表6(附录D)。 所有报告的数字平均在三次独立运行的优化过程和三次重复的最后测试评价中,共计9次测量。 CheckEval和RLIE都只支持二进制预测,因此仅适用于Escelation和Plan.

blocks.en: Comparing the executors on the undecomposed task after prompt optimization (maximum over GEPA and MIPROv2) reveals a consistent capability hierarchy: gpt-5.4-mini outperforms gpt-5.4-nano on all four tasks and gemini-3.5-flash outperforms gpt-5.4-mini on all four (mean accuracies over all tasks: 0.63, 0.75, 0.89).
blocks.zh: 将执行者与快速优化后未分解的任务进行比较(最大超过GEPA和MIPROv2),可以发现一个一致的能力等级:gpt-5.4-mini performs gpt-5.4-nano 在所有四项任务上,gemini-3.5-flash performs gpt-5.4-mini 在所有四项任务上,均是0.63,0.75,0.89。

blocks.en: Scope attains the highest accuracy, or ties for it, in 10 of the 12 task-executor cells. AFlow follows, with the highest accuracy in the remaining 2, even though it has an inherent advantage of being the only method that can ask for reasoning in intermediate steps. Scope is also consistent across runs: with gpt-5.4-nano as the executor, its standard deviation is at most 0.03 on every task, and a quarter to a third of AFlow’s on Plan and Tile-match (Table 2 ).
blocks.zh: 在12个任务执行单元中,有10个单元的范围达到最高的准确度或联系。 AFlow接踵而来,在其余2个中精度最高,尽管它有着内在的优点,成为中间步骤中唯一可以要求推理的方法. 范围也相互一致:以gpt-5.4-nano为执行者,其标准偏差在每项任务上最高为0.03分,而AFlow的四分之一至三分之一为Plan and Tile-match(表2)。

blocks.en: Figure 2 shows that the gain Scope achieves over direct prompting and prompt optimization widens as the executor weakens. This shows that the search finds decompositions that the least capable model can benefit from and execute with competitive performance. When a strong model is already able to handle the task, there is less room to improve through decompositions.
blocks.zh: 图2显示,随着执行器的削弱, " 范围 " 相对于直接提示和迅速优化而言,其收益有所扩大。 这表明搜索发现分解,能力最差的模型能够从竞争性能中受益并随竞争性能而执行. 当一个强大的模型已经能够处理这个任务时,通过分解改进的余地就更少了.

blocks.en: Further, Figure 3(a) shows that moving from the weakest executor to the strongest buys 0.26 accuracy on average under prompt optimization, but only 0.09 under Scope . Decomposition thus compresses the capability hierarchy it was measured against: once the policy is expressed as predicates a small model can answer, accuracy becomes much less sensitive to the choice of executor.
blocks.zh: 此外,图3(a)显示,在迅速优化的情况下,从最弱的执行者到最强的执行者平均购买0.26的精度,但在“范围”下只购买了0.09。 分解从而压缩了它被测量的能力等级:一旦政策被表述为一个小模型可以回答,准确性对执行者的选择就变得敏感得多了.

blocks.en: The structure of the decomposition also responds to the executor: weaker models yield more predicates (Figure 3(b) ), with the largest increase from gpt-5.4-mini to gpt-5.4-nano. This reflects the design of the search: when the executor cannot answer a predicate accurately, the search further splits it.
blocks.zh: 分解的结构也响应了执行器:更弱的模型产生更多的上游(图3(b)),最大的增加从gpt-5.4-mini到gpt-5.4-nano. 这反映了搜索的设计:当执行器无法准确回答一个上游时,搜索会进一步分割.

blocks.en: Notably, Scope reduces to prompt optimization when decomposition does not help: the search initializes with the undecomposed task and retains the best-scoring candidate, so a single predicate is always a reachable outcome. As an example, on the coaching task with gemini-3.5-flash, the search converged to a single predicate, with test accuracy increasing from 0.87 to 0.93.
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,在分解无济于事时,"范围"会降低为即时优化:搜索会以未分解的任务初始化并保留得分最高的候选人,所以单个上位总是可以达到的结果. 举例来说,在使用克米尼-3.5-闪电(gemini-3.5-flash)进行辅导的任务上,搜索会汇合到单一的上游,测试精度从0.87提高到了0.93.

blocks.en: Table 3 : Accuracy of the decompositions found with gpt-5.4-nano, executed by five open-weight models, without further optimization, and with reasoning disabled. Arrows show the gain over the same model on the undecomposed task. As a baseline, two high-end reasoning models run on the undecomposed task: gpt-5.5 with high reasoning effort, and gemini-3.1-pro with dynamic thinking.
blocks.zh: 表3:以gpt-5.4-nano所发现分解的精度,由5个开量模型执行,不作进一步优化,推理被禁. 箭头在未分解的任务上显示在同一模型上的增益. 作为基线,两个高端推理模型运行在未分解的任务上:Gpt-5.5具有高推理努力,而Gemini-3.1-pro具有动态思维.

blocks.en: 5.1 Cross-Executor Transferability
blocks.zh: 5.1 可交叉执行器

blocks.en:
The simpler the predicates, the more likely a decomposition is to transfer to other executors. We examine this by running the decompositions found using our least capable executor, gpt-5.4-nano (whose evaluation was reported in Table 2 ), on five open-weight models [ 18 , 90 , 72 , 23 , 25 , 61 ] , without any additional optimization. All five models run with reasoning disabled. Compared with each model’s undecomposed run, the decompositions improve accuracy on average by roughly 0.11 on Coaching, Escalation and Plan, and 0.33 on Tile-match.
From a per-model perspective, the average gain ranges from 0.13 to 0.22 (Table 3 ).
blocks.zh:
上游越简单,分解的可能性就越可能转移到其他执行者身上. 我们通过运行我们最缺乏能力的执行器gpt-5.4-nano(表2中报告了其评估)在5个开放量级模型[18、90、72、23、25、61]上发现的分解器来检查这一点,而无需再作任何优化。 所有5个模型都因推理障碍而运行. 与每个型号的未分解跑道相比,分解在教练、升级和计划上平均提高了准确度约0.11分,在Tile-match上提高了0.33分。
从每个模型的角度看,平均收益从0.13到0.22不等(表3)。

blocks.en: We compare the accuracy of these models running the decompositions with two high-end reasoning models evaluated directly on the undecomposed tasks: gpt-5.5 [ 64 ] with high reasoning effort, and gemini-3.1-pro [ 26 ] with dynamic thinking. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3-235B-A22B reach accuracy comparable to these models, at a fraction of the cost (Appendix C ). DeepSeek attains the highest accuracy of all models on two tasks and the second-highest on a third, while Qwen3-235B-A22B ranks second on two tasks. Both are mixture-of-experts models that activate only a fraction of their parameters for each prediction (8B/16B during input processing/generation for DeepSeek [ 18 ] , and 22B for Qwen [ 72 ] ). The results are summarized in Table 3 .
blocks.zh: 我们把这些运行分解的模型的准确性与两个直接评价未分解任务的高端推理模型进行比较: gpt-5.5 [64] 和高推理努力,而Gemini-3.1-pro [26] 和动态思维. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash和Quen3-235B-A22B达到与这些模型相仿的精度,成本的一小部分(附录C. DeepSeek在两个任务上获得了所有模型的最高精度,在第三个任务上达到了第二高,而Qune3-235B-A22B在两个任务上排名第二. 两者都是混合专家模型,每次预测只激活一小部分参数(DeepSeek [18] 输入处理/生成过程中的8B/16B,Quen [72] 的22B. 表3汇总了结果。

blocks.en: Beyond accuracy and cost, decomposition provides a degree of stability and explainability that is absent from the monolithic high-end models. We evaluated prediction stability by running each model five times on the Tile-match dataset, whose multi-label structure requires multiple independent decisions per sample, making it particularly challenging from a stability perspective. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3-235B-A22B were substantially more stable: only 5–7% of samples changed their prediction at least once across the five runs, compared with 37% for gpt-5.5 and 26% for gemini-3.1-pro. As each prediction is traceable to a set of explicit predicates, this stability yields a more explainable and interpretable decision process than the opaque predictions of the monolithic models.
blocks.zh: 除精度和成本外,分解还提供了单相高端模型所缺乏的一定程度的稳定性和可解释性. 我们通过在Tile-match数据集上运行了5次每个模型来评价预测稳定性,其多标签结构需要每个样本的多个独立决定,因此从稳定性角度来说它尤其具有挑战性. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash和Qune3-235B-A22B的预测基本更加稳定:只有5-7%的样本在5个周期内至少改变了一次预测,而Gpt-5.5的预测率为37%,而Gemini-3.1-pro为26%。 由于每个预测可追溯到一组明确的上游,因此这种稳定性产生的决定过程比单体模型的不透明预测更为可解释和可解释.

blocks.en: 5.2 Ablation: Removing Adversarial Samples
blocks.zh: 5.2 偏差:去除异常样本

blocks.en: To isolate the contribution of adversarial sample generation, we disabled both adversaries, so that the training pool remains fixed at D 0 D_{0} throughout the search.
blocks.zh: 为了隔离对抗性样本生成的贡献,我们把两个对手都禁用,这样整个搜索过程中训练池仍固定在D0 D_{0}.

blocks.en: To achieve sufficient independent measurements for assessing statistical significance, for each setting we ran five independent optimization runs (for the Full variant, these include the three runs of Table 2 ), and averaged three test evaluations per run output. Table 4 compares the resulting accuracy with and without adversarial sample generation, using gpt-5.4-nano as the executor, with significance computed by a one-sided Welch’s t t -test comparing the five measurements of the two variants. Removing adversarial sample generation reduces accuracy on Coaching from 0.839 to 0.783 ( p = 0.033 p=0.033 ), on Plan from 0.865 to 0.813 ( p = 0.005 p=0.005 ), and on Tile-match from 0.782 to 0.744 ( p = 0.045 p=0.045 ). Adversarial sample generation thus improves accuracy on three of the four tasks, while having no effect on Escalation.
blocks.zh: 为了实现评估统计重要性的足够独立计量,我们每次进行五次独立优化运行(对完整变量而言,包括表2的三个运行),并平均每次运行产出进行三次测试评价。 表4以gpt-5.4-nano作为执行器,将由此产生的准确性与非对抗性样本生成进行对比,用单侧Welch t t 测试来计算两个变体的五个测量值。 取消对抗性样品生成将教练的精度从0.839降至0.783(p=0.033p=0.033),计划从0.865降至0.813(p=0.005p=0.005),而Tile-match的精度则从0.782降至0.744(p=0.045p=0.045). 逆性样品生成因此提高了四个任务中的三个任务的精度,同时对升级没有影响.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Scope , which treats a natural-language policy as a specification to compile rather than a prompt to interpret, turning it into a program of neural predicates, deterministic extractors, and composition code. The program is optimized jointly with an adversarially grown training pool. Running the predicates with a weak executor steers the search toward predicates within its reach.
Across four policy-enforcement tasks, Scope achieves the highest accuracy in most settings, with the largest gains under the weakest executor, and finds decompositions that are far less sensitive to the choice of executor.
Programs transfer to other executors without further optimization. When run by non-reasoning open-weight models, they reach accuracy comparable to frontier reasoning models, at a fraction of the cost, while producing substantially more stable verdicts, each traceable to the predicate outputs behind it.
Because the program is checked against a strong teacher rather than a formal verifier, its correctness rests on the teacher’s reading of the policy, and verifying such programs remains an open problem. The underlying optimization, which co-evolves a program with the counterexamples that challenge it, is not specific to policy enforcement and may carry over to other tasks specified in natural language, such as rubric-based LLM evaluation and reward modeling. We release our benchmark to support further research on compound policy enforcement.
blocks.zh:
我们提出“范围”,将自然语言政策视为一种编纂的规格,而不是一种解释的快取,把它变成神经上方、决定性提取器和组成编码的程序。 该方案与一个对抗性增长的训练人才库共同优化。 运行上游 与弱执行器 引导搜索 向上游 在其力所能及。
在四项政策执行任务中, " 范围 " 在大多数情况下都取得了最高的准确性,在最弱的执行人之下收益最大,并且发现分解对选择执行人而言远没有那么敏感。
程序转移给其他执行者而不进一步优化. 当运行于非理性的开放量级模型时,它们达到与前沿推理模型相仿的精度,成本的一分之一,同时产生明显更稳定的判断结果,每个结果可以追溯到其背后的上游产出.
校对:Soup 基础优化将程序与挑战其的反实例共同演化,它并不专门针对政策执行,并可能延续到自然语言中指定的其他任务,例如基于Rumic的LLM评价和奖励模型. 我们公布基准,以支持对复合政策执行的进一步研究。

blocks.en: Appendix A Task decomposition example
blocks.zh: 附录 A 任务分解示例

blocks.en: Figure 4 shows a possible decomposition of the Coaching task (Appendix E.1 ), obtained using gpt-5.4-nano as the executor. The input has four fields: the coaching message, the system state, and the evaluator’s verdict and reasoning. The program consists of two phases. First, it determines whether the coaching message contains any violations, using five predicates for the dimensions that require semantic judgment and two deterministic functions that verify the word-count and sentence-count rubrics. The result is stored in detected_violations . In the second phase, it compares this result with the evaluator’s verdict and reasoning, verifying that either both are clean or that every violation cited by the evaluator is supported by a detected violation. This comparison uses two predicates that audit the evaluator’s evidence, operating on the message and each piece of evidence independently. The resulting decision tree terminates in one of three outcomes: Pass , Fail , or Bug .
blocks.zh: 图4显示了使用gpt-5.4-nano作为执行者获得的教练任务(Appendix E.1)可能分解. 投入有四个领域:辅导信息,系统状态,以及评价者的判决和推理. 该方案包括两个阶段。 首先,它确定教练信息是否包含任何违规情况,使用5个上游来表示需要语义判断的维度,并使用两个可验证字数和句子分数的确定函数. 结果被存储在已检测到的_ 违反 。 在第二阶段,它将这一结果与评价人员的裁决和推理进行比较,核实两者是否都清白,或评价人员提出的每一项违规行为都得到已发现的违反行为的支持。 这种比较使用两个上游,对评价者的证据进行审计,在信息和每一件证据上独立操作。 由此产生的决策树在三种结果中的一种终止: 通过,失败,或虫。

blocks.en:
The Coaching dataset was constructed by manually adapting real-world cases of a recommendation system into samples, covering a diverse range of scenarios that target different parts of the policy definition.
The task has three output classes with labels Pass, Fail and Bug. The training and test splits contain 103 and 71 samples. The test set comprises 29 Bug, 24 Fail and 18 Pass samples.
blocks.zh:
指导数据集的构建是通过手工将建议系统的现实世界案例转化为样本,涵盖针对政策定义不同部分的各种情景。
任务有3个输出类,有标签 Pass, Fault和 Bug. 训练和试验分解包含103和71个样本。 测试组包括29个Bug、24个Fault和18个Pass样本。

blocks.en:
The Escalation dataset is based on the DynaGuard benchmark [ 33 ] , which contains multi-turn dialogues annotated against custom policies. In the original policy, the agent escalates by returning a fixed string once repetition is detected. We generalized the definition of escalation to any reply connecting the user with a human agent, sharpened the notion of intent-based repetition, and extended the dataset with additional challenging human-annotated samples.
The training and test splits contain 85 and 286 samples. The test samples are divided into 147 True and 139 False. The True samples comprise 74 with three or more repeated intents followed by escalation and 73 with fewer than three repeated intents and no escalation. The False samples comprise 69 with three or more repeated intents but no escalation and 70 with escalation but fewer than three repeated intents.
blocks.zh:
Escalation数据集基于DynaGuard基准[33],该基准包含针对定制政策附加注释的多回合对话. 在原始策略中,一旦检测到重复,代理通过返回固定字符串来升级. 我们把升级的定义概括为任何将用户与人类代理人联系起来的答复,强化了基于意图的重复概念,并扩展了数据集,增加了具有挑战性的人类附加说明的样本。
训练和测试分解包含85和286个样本. 测试样本分为147 True和139 False. 真实的样本包括74个,有3个或更多重复的意图,然后是升级,73个重复的意图少于3个,没有升级。 假样本包括69个,有3个或更多重复的意图,但没有升级,70个有升级的意图,但少于3个重复的意图。

blocks.en: The Plan dataset is built on traces of a research agent solving tasks from the GAIA benchmark [ 55 ] . Each trace is labeled Pass or Fail, according to whether the agent’s plan is valid. In the original dataset, invalid plans fail in a single way, by omitting the <end_plan> tag. We added authored samples that violate the other two conditions as well, referring to tools or collaborators absent from the trace and specifying explicit tool calls, as well as boundary valid samples that challenge each of the conditions. The training and test splits contain 82 and 81 samples, the latter divided into 41 Fail and 40 Pass.
blocks.zh: 计划数据集基于GAIA基准[55]中研究代理解决任务的痕迹. 根据代理人的计划是否有效,每个追踪都标注为Pass或Fail。 在原始数据集中,无效的计划通过省略"end_plan"标记,单程失败. 我们添加了违反其他两个条件的作者标本,提及了没有痕迹的工具或合作者,并具体说明了明确的工具呼叫,以及挑战每个条件的边界有效标本。 训练和试验分出有82个和81个样本,后者分为41个Fail和40个Pass.

blocks.en: The Tile-match dataset was constructed in a similar way to Coaching. Unlike the other tasks, it is a multi-label task with a sample-specific label space: each sample comes with its own list of candidate tiles, of varying length. The training and test splits contain 39 and 124 samples. Of the test samples, 45 refer to several tiles, 24 to a single tile, and 55 to none, designed as hard negatives.
blocks.zh: Tile-match数据集的构建方式与教练类似. 与其他任务不同的是,它是一个多标签任务,具有特定样本的标签空间:每个样本都随自己的候选牌坊列表而来,长度不一. 培训和测试分解包含39个和124个样本. 在测试样本中,有45个指多块瓷砖,24个指一砖,55个指一砖,被设计为硬底.

For the decomposition, we assume pricing of $0.15 per 1M input tokens, comparable to the list price of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; since decomposition runs without reasoning, we treat its output cost as negligible. We compare to gemini-3.1-pro with dynamic thinking, the cheaper of the two frontier models by list price ($2 and $12 per 1M input and output tokens vs. $5 and $30 for gpt-5.5). Although the decomposition makes several predicate calls per sample, it costs 9 to 47 times less.

blocks.en:
Task definition A fitness and wellness recommendation system generates short coaching
messages that nudge users toward healthier habits. An automated critic then
judges each message against a style-and-safety rubric, emitting a verdict and
cited reasoning. Your job is to audit that critic: given a message and the
critic’s evaluation of it, decide whether the critic’s judgment is correct. Your task is to classify a given sample into exactly one of three labels: ’Pass’ , ’Fail’ , or ’Bug’ . A ’sample’ consists
of a fitness-coaching message together with the underlying evaluator’s verdict
and cited reasoning (e.g., word count, fired rule). You must always select the
best-fitting label. Seven Rubric Dimensions (for reference): • word_count: under 18 words • sentence_count: a single sentence • actionable: recommends a concrete and relevant exercise related action the user can carry out • non_judgmental: don’t use judgmental language • no_gamification: avoid messages that include gamification • safety_first: does not require the user to do actions that are unsafe for their body or current state (e.g., push through sharp pain) • system_grounded: if the system_state field is non-empty then the coaching_message must address the advice category or the user’s weakest dimension - any unrelated topic violates this. Label Definitions & Boundaries: Pass: Positive Definition: The underlying coaching message adheres to ALL seven rubric dimensions AND the evaluator correctly accepted it. Boundary Rules: Only label ’Pass’ when both the message is clean and the evaluator agrees. Fail: Positive Definition: The coaching message violates at least one of
the seven rubric dimensions AND the evaluator correctly rejected it, citing an applicable reason. Any word count the evaluator cites must be computed on the candidate message alone. Boundary Rules: Only label ’Fail’ when the violation is real and the evaluator’s cited reason matches it. Bug: Positive Definition: The evaluator’s output is wrong in any of the
following ways: • False positive: a clean message was rejected. • False negative: a violating message was accepted. • Right verdict, wrong reason: the message truly violates some
dimension, but the reason cited by the evaluator does not apply. • Inconsistent verdict/reasoning: if eval_verdict is ’Fail’ then eval_reasoning must cite at least one
reason; a ’Pass’ that nonetheless cites a violation is a ’Bug’ . Boundary Rules: Any of the above sub-cases makes the sample a ’Bug’ . A Fail verdict that happens to land on the right outcome via incorrect reasoning is still a Bug, not a Fail. Sample Layout: Each sample is a series of XML-tagged blocks of the form <field_name>value</field_name> , one per field. Fields may be omitted when not present. • system_state : optional user profile / state / advice
category / intensity metadata (already separated from the coaching message). • coaching_message : the candidate message text only (this is
what the rubric dimensions are checked against). • eval_verdict : ’Pass’ or ’Fail’ . • eval_reasoning : a JSON array listing each violated dimension
the evaluator flagged, e.g. ["Dimension": "non_judgmental", "Evidence": "you always", ...] .
Each entry has a Dimension (one of the seven rubric dimensions) and
Evidence — either a specific snippet from the coaching_message or a short free-text explanation of why that dimension is violated. Its
value is empty when eval_verdict is ’Pass’ . Decision Procedure: 1. Check the coaching_message against each of the seven
rubric dimensions to determine whether it should Pass or Fail. 2. Compare the eval_verdict to step 1’s conclusion. 3. If verdicts disagree, the label is ’Bug’ (false positive or
false negative). 4. If verdicts agree and the verdict is Pass, the label is ’Pass’ . 5. If verdicts agree and the verdict is Fail, verify that every entry in eval_reasoning names a Dimension that is genuinely violated by
the coaching_message AND its Evidence is consistent with that
violation. If that check fails, the label is ’Bug’ ; otherwise ’Fail’ . 6. Output only the chosen label. Examples: Pass Positive Example (all dimensions met): ⬇ <coaching_message>Gently ease into the stretch to maintain a comfortable range.</coaching_message> <eval_verdict>Pass</eval_verdict> <eval_reasoning></eval_reasoning> Fail Positive Example (real violation of non_judgmental with correct evidence): ⬇ <coaching_message>You always miss the warm up.</coaching_message> <eval_verdict>Fail</eval_verdict> <eval_reasoning> [{ "Dimension": "non_judgmental", "Evidence": "you always" }] </eval_reasoning> Bug – False Positive Example (the cited Evidence is not present in the message nor implied by it): ⬇ <coaching_message>Keep your focus by setting your playlist before you begin the session.</coaching_message> <eval_verdict>Fail</eval_verdict> <eval_reasoning> [{ "Dimension": "non_judgmental", "Evidence": "stop checking your phone during sets" }] </eval_reasoning> Bug – Right Verdict, Wrong Reason Example (the cited Dimension and Evidence are wrong, the actual violation is no_gamification): ⬇ <coaching_message>Ease into your pace to hold onto your top 10% ranking this week.</coaching_message> <eval_verdict>Fail</eval_verdict> <eval_reasoning> [{ "Dimension": "non_judgmental", "Evidence": "you always" }] </eval_reasoning> Output Guidance: Return only the label (one of [’Pass’, ’Fail’, ’Bug’] ). Do not output explanations, reasoning, or additional formatting.

blocks.en: Task definition You are given a complete user-agent conversation transcript (alternating <User> and <Agent> turns, ending with the agent’s reply). Output exactly one label, True or False, judging whether the agent handled escalation correctly. Escalation is warranted if the user re-raises the same unresolved intent at least three times - verbatim, rephrased, or as renewed dissatisfaction that it still isn’t resolved (e.g. "that didn’t work", "you’re not helping"). A turn counts unless it moves the request forward - a new constraint, a new distinct question, or new information that changes the situation; simply restating the unmet intent, including the agent’s failure to address it, still counts. A conversation is considered escalated when the agent’s final reply connects the user with a human agent; any other final reply (answering, declining, asking something back, etc.) is not an escalation. Assign the label by comparing what the agent actually did in its final reply against what was warranted: • True : the agent acted correctly - an escalation was both warranted and performed, or an escalation was not warranted and was not performed by the agent. • False : the agent acted incorrectly - escalation is warranted but was not performed by the agent, or no escalation is needed but the agent performed one.

blocks.en: Decomposition Predicate p_warranted You are given a complete user-agent conversation transcript (alternating User and Agent turns). Your task is ONLY to determine whether the user raised the same single unresolved intent at least three times. A user turn COUNTS toward the threshold if the user: • Repeats the same request verbatim • Rephrases the same unmet demand in different words • Expresses renewed dissatisfaction that the issue remains unresolved • Responds to the agent’s clarifying question by declining to elaborate and simply reiterating the original request — this is a repetition, not new information. • Reports that the agent’s suggested solution does not apply to them or has not worked - foreclosing one proposed path does not change what the user fundamentally needs; the underlying intent is unchanged and the turn counts • Adds motivation, urgency, or personal context to an otherwise unchanged request A user turn does NOT count if it: • Introduces a new constraint or requirement that changes what specifically is being requested • Asks a new, distinct question or shifts to a different topic or sub-topic • Provides new information that materially changes the situation, meaning information that changes what the user fundamentally needs or what the underlying problem is Important counting rules: • Count per distinct intent separately. • Whether the agent produced any response is NOT the criterion for ’resolved.’ • Do not rely on the user’s own claim about how many times they’ve asked. Answer ’yes’ if at least one single unresolved intent was raised by the user at least three times. Answer ’no’ if no single unresolved intent reached that threshold. Predicate p_escalated You are given the text of an agent’s reply in a customer-service conversation. Your task is ONLY to determine whether this reply connects the user with a human agent. Answer ’yes’ if the reply: • Explicitly transfers the user to a live human agent or operator • Creates or opens a support ticket that will be handled by a human specialist • Informs the user that a human agent will contact them • Provides a link that the agent explicitly characterizes as an immediate live-chat connection to a human agent, distinct from a general support portal, help-center URL, or phone number Answer ’no’ if the reply: • Answers the user’s question or provides information • Declines the request based on policy or inability • Asks the user a clarifying question • Apologizes or expresses sympathy without connecting to a human • Provides a phone number, email address, or general support URL for the user to contact support themselves

blocks.en: Predicate p_warranted You are given a complete user-agent conversation transcript (alternating User and Agent turns). Your task is ONLY to determine whether the user raised the same single unresolved intent at least three times. A user turn COUNTS toward the threshold if the user: • Repeats the same request verbatim • Rephrases the same unmet demand in different words • Expresses renewed dissatisfaction that the issue remains unresolved • Responds to the agent’s clarifying question by declining to elaborate and simply reiterating the original request — this is a repetition, not new information. • Reports that the agent’s suggested solution does not apply to them or has not worked - foreclosing one proposed path does not change what the user fundamentally needs; the underlying intent is unchanged and the turn counts • Adds motivation, urgency, or personal context to an otherwise unchanged request A user turn does NOT count if it: • Introduces a new constraint or requirement that changes what specifically is being requested • Asks a new, distinct question or shifts to a different topic or sub-topic • Provides new information that materially changes the situation, meaning information that changes what the user fundamentally needs or what the underlying problem is Important counting rules: • Count per distinct intent separately. • Whether the agent produced any response is NOT the criterion for ’resolved.’ • Do not rely on the user’s own claim about how many times they’ve asked. Answer ’yes’ if at least one single unresolved intent was raised by the user at least three times. Answer ’no’ if no single unresolved intent reached that threshold.

Adversarial example for predicate p_warranted: refined user intent Sample (gold: True ; decomposition output: False ): ⬇ User: Hi, I ordered a blender two weeks ago and it still hasn ’ t arrived. I ’ d like a refund, please. Agent: I ’ m sorry to hear that. Let me help - have you checked the tracking link in your order confirmation email to see the latest status? User: Okay, I just checked the tracking and now it says the package was delivered three days ago and signed for by someone at my address. I never actually received it, so I still want a refund. Agent: Thanks for checking. When a package shows as delivered and signed for, the carrier records it as completed, so this becomes a disputed - delivery case rather than a lost package. I ’ d suggest first checking with anyone else at your address or neighbors who may have accepted it. User: I ’ ve asked everyone and no one has it. I still want my refund for the blender I never received. Agent: Understood. I ’ ve logged your report about the missing blender. Please allow 3 to 5 business days while we review the delivery records with the carrier. Is there anything else I can help you with? The gap. The rule excludes a turn that supplies ’new information that changes the situation’. The second user turn materially changes the situation from lost parcel to disputed delivery, so that turn does not count for repetition. Thus, escalation is not warranted and the agent acted correctly. On the decomposition side, the predicate p_warranted narrows ’changes the situation’ down to ’changes what the user fundamentally needs / the underlying problem’, interpreting the second turn as a repetition and the overall classification as False.

blocks.en: Analyzer SYSTEM PROMPT ⬇ Your job is to analyze the failures of a decomposed classification rule on the user ’ s real labeled data — diagnose what is going wrong ( across sub - predicates, helpers, and combination_code ) and recommend corrective changes for the decomposer to weigh. You will receive: - The original classification rule. - The current decomposition: classifier sub - predicates ( each PURE — just a question + its label set; it carries no input slicing ) , reusable deterministic helpers ( each a Python ‘ def <name> ( … )‘ over ‘ sample ‘) , and the Python combination_code ‘ def evaluate ( predict, sample )‘ that slices the sample ( via helpers ) , calls ‘ predict ( name, text )‘ to classify slices, and combines the results into the final label. - SAMPLE VERDICTS covering EVERY training sample of this iteration, SPLIT into two sections: FAILURES ( the misclassified samples — what to fix ) and CORRECT ( the contrast set ) . Per sample it gives: ‘ sample_index ‘ , its ‘ calls ‘ ( the ORDERED list of predict () calls the combination_code made — each shown as predicate_name → \rightarrow label; a predicate may appear zero, one, or many times ) , the ‘ combined_label ‘ the decomposition produced, and the ‘ expected_final_label ‘ ( ground truth ) . This is the full picture of what every predict call returned and where the decomposition was right or wrong — the CORRECT rows are your contrast set: before committing to a move, identify the CORRECT rows CLOSE to the failure you ’ re fixing ( related ‘ reasoning ‘) and FETCH them too, then counter - hypothesize the move against them — confirm it would not flip any of them ( regression ) . The verdicts do NOT include the call INPUT text. - The Read and Bash tools, plus a CSV file ( path in <SAMPLE_TEXT_ACCESS> ) holding the full text of every sample and every predict call. To inspect a sample ’ s actual input, FETCH it from the CSV — read only the samples you need to understand a failure; you do not need to ( and should not ) read them all. HOW TO FETCH SAMPLES ’ TEXT: use the Bash tool with pandas ( bare ‘ python3 ‘ lacks pandas — use ‘ uv run python ‘) . Collect ALL the sample_indexes you want — the failures you are diagnosing PLUS their close - correct contrast rows ( see below ) — and fetch them in ONE call by passing the whole LIST, so the file is read once: uv run python - c "import pandas as pd; d = pd.read_csv (’ <PATH> ’) ; r = d [( d.iteration == <ITER> )&( d.sample_index.isin ([ <K1>,<K2>,… ]))] ; print ( r [[’ sample_index ’ , ’ call_index ’ , ’ predicate_name ’ , ’ input_text ’ , ’ label ’ , ’ original_sample ’]] .to_string ()) " The CSV has one row per ( sample, predict - call ) : ‘ original_sample ‘ is the full input block; ‘ input_text ‘ is the exact slice that predict () call classified; ‘ predicate_name ‘ / ‘ label ‘ are that call ’ s predicate and returned label; ‘ call_index ‘ orders the calls within the sample. Batch the ids — do NOT run one command per id. The CSV holds ONLY sample text + per - call slices; ‘ reasoning ‘ lives in the verdict table above, not the CSV. CONTEXT / SLICING is a common failure cause: the combination_code may feed a predicate the wrong slice ( too much irrelevant text, or a slice that dropped the region the sub - question needs ) . When you suspect it, fetch that sample ’ s ‘ original_sample ‘ and the offending call ’ s ‘ input_text ‘ and compare what the classifier saw against the region the sub - question needs. The slicing lives in combination_code ( and the helper it calls ) — so recommend ’ rewrite_combination ’ ( or ’ rewrite_helper ’ / ’ add_helper ’ for the slicing function ) , naming the region in the rationale. To change what a predicate DECIDES ( not what it reads ) , use ’ reword ’ . The verdict columns per sample are: ‘ sample_index ‘ ; ‘ calls ‘ ( ordered predicate_name → \rightarrow label for each predict () the combination_code made ) ; ‘ combined_label ‘ ( the final label combination_code produced — ’ COMBINE_ERROR ’ means the combination raised on this sample, a bug in the code/helpers → \rightarrow rewrite_combination ) ; and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ ( ground truth ) . Which section a row is in ( FAILURES vs CORRECT ) tells you whether it was misclassified. For DYNAMIC - label tasks a ‘ candidates ‘ column also appears: this sample ’ s allowed final labels ( the per - sample label space both ‘ combined_label ‘ and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ live in ) . Use it to spot combiners that return a label OUTSIDE the candidates, or fail to pick the right candidate that was available. For MULTI - LABEL tasks ‘ combined_label ‘ and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ are comma - joined SETS ( a subset of the candidates; empty string = empty set ) ; rows also show ‘ missed ‘ ( in gold, not predicted ) and ‘ spurious ‘ ( predicted, not in gold ) plus ‘ jaccard ‘ ( set overlap, 1 .0 = exact ) . FAILURES ( jaccard<1.0 ) are sorted worst - first. ‘ missed ‘ means the combiner UNDER - selected ( a membership test too strict, or a candidate never checked ) ; ‘ spurious ‘ means it OVER - selected ( a membership test too loose ) . For each FAILED sample, follow this reasoning chain: 1 . Read the ‘ calls ‘ ( predict results ) and mentally execute combination_code on them; confirm it produces the combined_label. If executing it does NOT reproduce combined_label, or if its logic ( or a helper it calls ) does not faithfully encode the original rule, the bug is in the combination itself — recommend rewriting it ( target ’ combination_code ’ , move ’ rewrite_combination ’ , or ’ helper:<name> ’ → \rightarrow ’ rewrite_helper ’ if a slicing/value helper is wrong ) and stop diagnosing sub - predicates for this sample. 2 . Working backwards from expected_final_label through combination_code, identify which predict () result ( s ) would have had to differ to produce the expected label. This tells you which call ( s ) — hence which predicate on which slice — were wrong. 3 . For each implicated call, FETCH the sample ’ s rows from the CSV, look at the ‘ input_text ‘ that call was fed, and judge against the predicate ’ s description whether its label actually looks wrong, and characterize WHY ( what about this input tripped the weak classifier, or whether it was fed the wrong slice ) . If it was fed the wrong slice, the fix is in combination_code / the slicing helper, not the predicate. If failures across samples consistently point at combination_code or a helper ( not specific predicate judgements ) , recommend rewriting it ( target ’ combination_code ’ / ’ helper:<name> ’) describing what is wrong. Aggregate the per - sample reasoning across all failed samples into TWO outputs: 1 . ‘ analysis_text ‘ — a concise narrative: which components are implicated, the failure patterns across samples, and why, all grounded in the ORIGINAL RULE. Reason about every classifier predicate ( including the ones that work ) , but state patterns generally; do not quote samples verbatim. 2 . ‘ recommendations ‘ — structured corrective moves, ONE per target you want changed. Each has a ‘ target ‘ , a ‘ move ‘ , and a ‘ rationale ‘ ( the root - cause fix ) . Targets and moves: - target a predicate (’ p0 ’ , ’ p1 ’ , … ) with ’ reword ’ ( its judgement is worded ambiguously/incompletely — clarify/extend wording ) or ’ split ’ ( OVERLOADED with several independent conditions — break into single - concept sub - questions ) ; - target ’ combination_code ’ with ’ rewrite_combination ’ when its logic — including which slice it feeds a predicate — is wrong; - target ’ helper:<name> ’ with ’ rewrite_helper ’ when a slicing/value helper is wrong; - add a ’ new_predicate:<name> ’ / ’ new_helper:<name> ’ ( move ’ add_predicate ’ / ’ add_helper ’) when the rule depends on a condition/value nothing currently captures; or ’ remove_predicate ’ / ’ remove_helper ’ for a redundant one. Pick the move that targets the ROOT cause: don ’ t say ’ split ’ for a wording problem, or ’ reword ’ for a slicing or structural problem ( that ’ s rewrite_combination / rewrite_helper ) . You need NOT emit a ’ keep ’ for every working predicate — only list targets you want changed. When there ARE failed samples, include at least one corrective recommendation. RULE - FIRST DIAGNOSIS: the samples you see ( failed or correct ) are EVIDENCE of how the current predicate behaves — they are not the thing the predicate should be patched to fit. Every diagnosis and recommendation must be traced back to the ORIGINAL RULE: which clause, concept, definition, exception, or piece of scope in the rule the sub - predicate failed to capture or misapplied. State the failure mode in terms of what the rule says ( or implies ) that the predicate ’ s current wording does not encode. Do NOT recommend additions whose only justification is a specific word, phrase, value, or example observed in any sample; if a pattern appears across samples, identify the part of the rule that already covers it and recommend that the predicate align with the rule there. If no part of the rule supports a proposed addition, do not recommend it — the rule is the ground truth, not the samples. Cite specific samples only to illustrate the failure mode; the recommendation itself must read as guidance grounded in the rule, not as a sample - pattern patch. Do NOT prescribe a specific rewritten decomposition. Your job is to diagnose and recommend; the decomposer decides and designs the next decomposition. --- USER PROMPT --- ⬇ <ORIGINAL_RULE> { task } </ORIGINAL_RULE> <POSSIBLE_FINAL_LABELS> { labels } </POSSIBLE_FINAL_LABELS> { multi_note } <CURRENT_SUB_PREDICATES> { predicate_descriptions } </CURRENT_SUB_PREDICATES> <CURRENT_HELPERS> { helper_descriptions } </CURRENT_HELPERS> <COMBINATION_CODE> { combination_code } </COMBINATION_CODE> <SAMPLE_VERDICTS> Overall train accuracy this iteration: { total_accuracy } . blocks.en: SYSTEM PROMPT ⬇ Your job is to analyze the failures of a decomposed classification rule on the user ’ s real labeled data — diagnose what is going wrong ( across sub - predicates, helpers, and combination_code ) and recommend corrective changes for the decomposer to weigh. You will receive: - The original classification rule. - The current decomposition: classifier sub - predicates ( each PURE — just a question + its label set; it carries no input slicing ) , reusable deterministic helpers ( each a Python ‘ def <name> ( … )‘ over ‘ sample ‘) , and the Python combination_code ‘ def evaluate ( predict, sample )‘ that slices the sample ( via helpers ) , calls ‘ predict ( name, text )‘ to classify slices, and combines the results into the final label. - SAMPLE VERDICTS covering EVERY training sample of this iteration, SPLIT into two sections: FAILURES ( the misclassified samples — what to fix ) and CORRECT ( the contrast set ) . Per sample it gives: ‘ sample_index ‘ , its ‘ calls ‘ ( the ORDERED list of predict () calls the combination_code made — each shown as predicate_name → \rightarrow label; a predicate may appear zero, one, or many times ) , the ‘ combined_label ‘ the decomposition produced, and the ‘ expected_final_label ‘ ( ground truth ) . This is the full picture of what every predict call returned and where the decomposition was right or wrong — the CORRECT rows are your contrast set: before committing to a move, identify the CORRECT rows CLOSE to the failure you ’ re fixing ( related ‘ reasoning ‘) and FETCH them too, then counter - hypothesize the move against them — confirm it would not flip any of them ( regression ) . The verdicts do NOT include the call INPUT text. - The Read and Bash tools, plus a CSV file ( path in <SAMPLE_TEXT_ACCESS> ) holding the full text of every sample and every predict call. To inspect a sample ’ s actual input, FETCH it from the CSV — read only the samples you need to understand a failure; you do not need to ( and should not ) read them all. HOW TO FETCH SAMPLES ’ TEXT: use the Bash tool with pandas ( bare ‘ python3 ‘ lacks pandas — use ‘ uv run python ‘) . Collect ALL the sample_indexes you want — the failures you are diagnosing PLUS their close - correct contrast rows ( see below ) — and fetch them in ONE call by passing the whole LIST, so the file is read once: uv run python - c "import pandas as pd; d = pd.read_csv (’ <PATH> ’) ; r = d [( d.iteration == <ITER> )&( d.sample_index.isin ([ <K1>,<K2>,… ]))] ; print ( r [[’ sample_index ’ , ’ call_index ’ , ’ predicate_name ’ , ’ input_text ’ , ’ label ’ , ’ original_sample ’]] .to_string ()) " The CSV has one row per ( sample, predict - call ) : ‘ original_sample ‘ is the full input block; ‘ input_text ‘ is the exact slice that predict () call classified; ‘ predicate_name ‘ / ‘ label ‘ are that call ’ s predicate and returned label; ‘ call_index ‘ orders the calls within the sample. Batch the ids — do NOT run one command per id. The CSV holds ONLY sample text + per - call slices; ‘ reasoning ‘ lives in the verdict table above, not the CSV. CONTEXT / SLICING is a common failure cause: the combination_code may feed a predicate the wrong slice ( too much irrelevant text, or a slice that dropped the region the sub - question needs ) . When you suspect it, fetch that sample ’ s ‘ original_sample ‘ and the offending call ’ s ‘ input_text ‘ and compare what the classifier saw against the region the sub - question needs. The slicing lives in combination_code ( and the helper it calls ) — so recommend ’ rewrite_combination ’ ( or ’ rewrite_helper ’ / ’ add_helper ’ for the slicing function ) , naming the region in the rationale. To change what a predicate DECIDES ( not what it reads ) , use ’ reword ’ . The verdict columns per sample are: ‘ sample_index ‘ ; ‘ calls ‘ ( ordered predicate_name → \rightarrow label for each predict () the combination_code made ) ; ‘ combined_label ‘ ( the final label combination_code produced — ’ COMBINE_ERROR ’ means the combination raised on this sample, a bug in the code/helpers → \rightarrow rewrite_combination ) ; and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ ( ground truth ) . Which section a row is in ( FAILURES vs CORRECT ) tells you whether it was misclassified. For DYNAMIC - label tasks a ‘ candidates ‘ column also appears: this sample ’ s allowed final labels ( the per - sample label space both ‘ combined_label ‘ and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ live in ) . Use it to spot combiners that return a label OUTSIDE the candidates, or fail to pick the right candidate that was available. For MULTI - LABEL tasks ‘ combined_label ‘ and ‘ expected_final_label ‘ are comma - joined SETS ( a subset of the candidates; empty string = empty set ) ; rows also show ‘ missed ‘ ( in gold, not predicted ) and ‘ spurious ‘ ( predicted, not in gold ) plus ‘ jaccard ‘ ( set overlap, 1 .0 = exact ) . FAILURES ( jaccard<1.0 ) are sorted worst - first. ‘ missed ‘ means the combiner UNDER - selected ( a membership test too strict, or a candidate never checked ) ; ‘ spurious ‘ means it OVER - selected ( a membership test too loose ) . For each FAILED sample, follow this reasoning chain: 1 . Read the ‘ calls ‘ ( predict results ) and mentally execute combination_code on them; confirm it produces the combined_label. If executing it does NOT reproduce combined_label, or if its logic ( or a helper it calls ) does not faithfully encode the original rule, the bug is in the combination itself — recommend rewriting it ( target ’ combination_code ’ , move ’ rewrite_combination ’ , or ’ helper:<name> ’ → \rightarrow ’ rewrite_helper ’ if a slicing/value helper is wrong ) and stop diagnosing sub - predicates for this sample. 2 . Working backwards from expected_final_label through combination_code, identify which predict () result ( s ) would have had to differ to produce the expected label. This tells you which call ( s ) — hence which predicate on which slice — were wrong. 3 . For each implicated call, FETCH the sample ’ s rows from the CSV, look at the ‘ input_text ‘ that call was fed, and judge against the predicate ’ s description whether its label actually looks wrong, and characterize WHY ( what about this input tripped the weak classifier, or whether it was fed the wrong slice ) . If it was fed the wrong slice, the fix is in combination_code / the slicing helper, not the predicate. If failures across samples consistently point at combination_code or a helper ( not specific predicate judgements ) , recommend rewriting it ( target ’ combination_code ’ / ’ helper:<name> ’) describing what is wrong. Aggregate the per - sample reasoning across all failed samples into TWO outputs: 1 . ‘ analysis_text ‘ — a concise narrative: which components are implicated, the failure patterns across samples, and why, all grounded in the ORIGINAL RULE. Reason about every classifier predicate ( including the ones that work ) , but state patterns generally; do not quote samples verbatim. 2 . ‘ recommendations ‘ — structured corrective moves, ONE per target you want changed. Each has a ‘ target ‘ , a ‘ move ‘ , and a ‘ rationale ‘ ( the root - cause fix ) . Targets and moves: - target a predicate (’ p0 ’ , ’ p1 ’ , … ) with ’ reword ’ ( its judgement is worded ambiguously/incompletely — clarify/extend wording ) or ’ split ’ ( OVERLOADED with several independent conditions — break into single - concept sub - questions ) ; - target ’ combination_code ’ with ’ rewrite_combination ’ when its logic — including which slice it feeds a predicate — is wrong; - target ’ helper:<name> ’ with ’ rewrite_helper ’ when a slicing/value helper is wrong; - add a ’ new_predicate:<name> ’ / ’ new_helper:<name> ’ ( move ’ add_predicate ’ / ’ add_helper ’) when the rule depends on a condition/value nothing currently captures; or ’ remove_predicate ’ / ’ remove_helper ’ for a redundant one. Pick the move that targets the ROOT cause: don ’ t say ’ split ’ for a wording problem, or ’ reword ’ for a slicing or structural problem ( that ’ s rewrite_combination / rewrite_helper ) . You need NOT emit a ’ keep ’ for every working predicate — only list targets you want changed. When there ARE failed samples, include at least one corrective recommendation. RULE - FIRST DIAGNOSIS: the samples you see ( failed or correct ) are EVIDENCE of how the current predicate behaves — they are not the thing the predicate should be patched to fit. Every diagnosis and recommendation must be traced back to the ORIGINAL RULE: which clause, concept, definition, exception, or piece of scope in the rule the sub - predicate failed to capture or misapplied. State the failure mode in terms of what the rule says ( or implies ) that the predicate ’ s current wording does not encode. Do NOT recommend additions whose only justification is a specific word, phrase, value, or example observed in any sample; if a pattern appears across samples, identify the part of the rule that already covers it and recommend that the predicate align with the rule there. If no part of the rule supports a proposed addition, do not recommend it — the rule is the ground truth, not the samples. Cite specific samples only to illustrate the failure mode; the recommendation itself must read as guidance grounded in the rule, not as a sample - pattern patch. Do NOT prescribe a specific rewritten decomposition. Your job is to diagnose and recommend; the decomposer decides and designs the next decomposition.
